Years ago, MacBook came with a slot that worked with a cable lock to secure the computer to a desk leg or similar fixed object. Such accessories were handy when you stepped away from your laptop briefly to order another drink at a coffee shop counter.

Those slots have long disappeared, but adapters now exist that let you add a security lock to a MacBook Neo, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro…

If you remember that recessed security slot on the side of a MacBook, you’re probably a long-time MacBook user. Those slots were designed for a T-shaped accessory that slid into the slot and locked in place with a 90-degree turn. The most common design came with a steel cable that could be threaded through a desk leg, and was quite popular in coffee shops and libraries.

CompuLock is now reviving the concept with an adapter that fits on a corner or edge of a MacBook, allowing you to attach a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece design and screws securely onto the MacBook.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version alongside the existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It must be stressed that this kind of lock has always been a very low level of security measure, designed only to stop someone from grabbing your MacBook and running off in the few seconds you’re not paying attention. I felt reassured using it in a smaller coffee shop because I could still see my table when I went to the counter to order another tea, but I would never rely on it alone to let my MacBook out of sight.

The adapter sells for $70, which is not cheap, and the cable lock itself still needs to be purchased separately; however, if you happen to have an old lock lying in a drawer, you might as well dig it out and put it to use again.
